rationale: Consumers care about it most and it is the most expensive to measure: it needs a reference. Weighted low on purpose so that a proxy is not mistaken for the real thing.
Cheapest high-value dimension to measure, and the first thing a consumer notices. The 2025 regression from 4.7% to 15.5% nulls is the strongest single signal in the lab.
Domain, code-set and referential rules. High weight because a violation here breaks joins downstream, not just a report.
Arithmetic and cross-field agreement. High weight because it is the dimension most often reported as 'the data is wrong' by consumers.
Lowest weight: gaps in location coverage degrade an analysis but rarely break it. Raise it for any dataset whose purpose is geographic.
Latency between event and availability. Weighted above coverage because a late dataset can be unusable regardless of how complete it is.
Entity-level duplication matters, but row-level uniqueness is usually a property of the key you chose. Weighted below the structural dimensions for that reason.
